title: Server Components and Client Components
description: Understand the mental model behind React Server Components, when to use 'use client', and how to compose both types safely.

data.text: React Server Components (RSC) change the question from *'where should I fetch?'* to *'where should I render?'*. A **Server Component** runs only on the server. It can read files, query databases, and keep secrets safe. A **Client Component** runs in the browser. It handles clicks, keyboard input, and state with `useState` or `useEffect`.
The hard part is knowing which boundary to draw. A good rule is: **default to Server Components**, and only add `'use client'` when you need interactivity, browser APIs, or React hooks.

items: A Server Component can import and render a Client Component.
A Client Component cannot import a Server Component as a child.
Pass data from Server to Client via props, not the other way around.

data.title: Common mistake
data.text: Adding `'use client'` at the top of every file out of habit. That turns the whole tree into client-side JavaScript, increasing bundle size and losing the performance benefit of Server Components.

data.title: Server Component fetching data
data.content: A page that fetches data on the server and passes it to a client component.

cards.title: Server Component
cards.description: Rendered on the server; no client JS. Great for data fetching, reading files, and accessing backend resources directly.

cards.title: Client Component
cards.description: Rendered on the client; enables interactivity. Use when you need `useState`, event handlers, or browser APIs.

items.text: Does this component use useState, useEffect, or event handlers?
items.hint: If yes, mark it as a Client Component.

items.text: Does this component fetch data or read from the filesystem?
items.hint: Keep it as a Server Component.

items.text: Can I lift the interactive part into a smaller child component?
items.hint: Prefer this over marking the whole tree client-side.

data.title: Key takeaway
points: Server Components run on the server and send HTML to the client.
Client Components add interactivity via browser JavaScript.
Compose them by passing data down from server to client, not the reverse.
data.takeaway: Think of Server Components as your default, and Client Components as opt-in islands of interactivity.
